subject: physical-education
title: Guided practice B: programming strength and mobility into a wider plan
focus: programming strength and mobility into a wider plan
essentialQuestion: How do I make a movement better before I make it heavier or faster?
privacySafeScenario: Build a technique-first strength and mobility progression, document the criteria for advancing each movement, and show a completed progression with the criteria met.
studentTask: Learner applies programming strength and mobility into a wider plan in a new situation at a self-set intensity and records what they did, noticed, and would adjust.
knowledgeCheck: In one concise response, explain the key idea behind programming strength and mobility into a wider plan and name one adjustment for the next session.
completionCriteria: The learner completes or fully describes the programming strength and mobility into a wider plan task using a version their body and setting allow.
The learner gives a cue, principle, tactic, or documented process rather than an unexplained result.
The learner self-assesses against the stated criteria and identifies one next adjustment.
adaptationChoices: Every movement has a seated, supported, reduced-range, and unloaded version. Advancement criteria are set by control and range, never by load lifted relative to any other person.
extensionChallenge: Apply programming strength and mobility into a wider plan under a new constraint, in a different activity, or teach the cue to someone else — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
Every movement has a seated, supported, reduced-range, and unloaded version. Advancement criteria are set by control and range, never by load lifted relative to any other person.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice or try one safe, optional example of programming strength and mobility into a wider plan in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
